title: Jagannath rides out
hook: a carver's closed door, a god left unfinished, and the lord of the world who leaves his temple once a year for everyone
carry: the lord of the world comes out to everyone
tomorrow: who counts as family? an old line answers in two words.

segments.voice: Yesterday, Arjuna's bow slipped, and Krishna answered with karmany eva. Karma yoga: do the work, offer it to Krishna. Today, a join hidden in a name, and a god who goes out into the street.
screen: `DO THE WORK. OFFER IT TO KRISHNA.`

segments.voice: As Puri tells it, King Indradyumna is shown in a dream that a holy log will wash up on the shore. It does. But no carver can cut it, until an old craftsman appears and says he'll make the images, on one condition: lock him in, and no one opens the door until he's done. Days pass behind the door, with the sound of carving. Then the sound stops. The queen fears the old man has died, and the king opens the door early. The carver is gone. The images stand there unfinished, with no hands and no feet. And the king is told in a dream: worship them just as they are.
screen: `A LOG FROM THE SEA.` → `DON'T OPEN THE DOOR.` → `THE CARVING STOPS.` → `UNFINISHED. WORSHIP THEM AS THEY ARE.`

segments.voice: That's how Jagannath of Puri came to look the way he does: round eyes, a wooden face, short arms. His name has a join in it. Jagat, the world, plus natha, lord. Before the n, the t got ready and turned into an n too: Jagannath, lord of the world. Most days he's inside the great temple at Puri, and not everyone may enter it. Even so, there's an image of him at the Lion Gate called Patitapavana, savior of the fallen, for those who can't go in. But once a year, at Rath Yatra, he comes out. Jagannath, his brother Balabhadra and his sister Subhadra are carried out and ride huge wooden chariots down the Grand Road, to the Gundicha temple, and stay about a week. Anyone at all can see him in the street, and that seeing has a name: darshan, to see God and be seen by him. Devotees say even one glimpse of him on the chariot is a blessing, and anyone can take hold of the ropes and pull. Before the chariots roll, the king of Puri sweeps the chariot floor with a golden broom, a king cleaning for the lord of the world. The teaching: God doesn't wait only behind temple walls for the right people. Once a year, he comes out to all of them, unfinished hands and all.
screen: `JAGAT + NATHA = JAGANNATH.` · `LORD OF THE WORLD.` · `PATITAPAVANA: SAVIOR OF THE FALLEN.` · `RATH YATRA: DARSHAN FOR ALL.` · `ANYONE CAN PULL THE ROPE.` · then, large: `THE LORD OF THE WORLD COMES OUT TO EVERYONE.`

segments.voice: Picture the Grand Road: the crowd, the drums, three chariots, ropes thick as an arm. Picture taking hold of a rope beside a stranger. If you pray, say softly, Jai Jagannath. If you don't, think of one person who usually stays outside the room you're in, and one small way to bring them in this week. Then let the picture go, and breathe.
Sandhi plainly: today, a t that gets ready for the n beside it. The world is still inside Jagannath.
Your line: the lord of the world comes out to everyone. Unfinished hands, and a rope for anyone. Rest easy.

howItsDone: At Rath Yatra in Puri, Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra ride three chariots to the Gundicha temple and anyone may pull the ropes; the king of Puri sweeps the chariots first. Rath Yatras are now also held in cities around the world.

fork.setup: a friend asks why a god would leave his temple and ride through crowded streets. what does Rath Yatra teach?
options: the lord of the world comes out so everyone, inside or outside the temple, can see him and pull the rope.
the temple needs cleaning, so the images are moved out of the way.
it's a parade for tourists; the real worship is only inside.
fork.reveal: Jagannath means lord of the world. once a year he leaves the temple, and anyone at all may see him and take the rope. even the king sweeps the chariot first.

original.note: Sanskrit: jagannātha, lord of the world; jagat + nātha, the t turned into n before the n.

trapdoor: what you thought: Jagannath's round-eyed image is just a folk style.
what it means: Puri tells of images left unfinished and worshipped as they are, of a lord of the world who rides out at Rath Yatra so anyone can have his darshan.

what a scholar hears: jagat + nātha with a final stop nasalized before a nasal (Ashtadhyayi 8.4.45); the Indradyumna legend in the Purushottama Kshetra Mahatmya and Odia tellings, which vary in detail.
recall: act fully, offer the fruit to Krishna

chat.meaning: Jagannath, jagat plus natha, is lord of the world. At Rath Yatra he comes out of his temple so anyone at all can have his darshan and take the rope.

Jagannath.meaning: lord of the world, worshipped at Puri

Puri.meaning: a temple town on the coast of Odisha

Rath Yatra.meaning: the chariot festival, when Jagannath rides out

Indradyumna.meaning: the king in Puri's story of the carving

Subhadra.meaning: Jagannath's sister, who rides with him

darshan.meaning: seeing God, and being seen by him

sources.ref: The Indradyumna legend of Jagannath (the log from the sea, the carver behind closed doors, the images left unfinished): Purushottama Kshetra Mahatmya (Skanda Purana) and Odia tellings, which vary in detail

Rath Yatra at Puri (three chariots to the Gundicha temple; the ropes; darshan of the deities on the chariots; chhera pahara, the king sweeping the chariots); the Patitapavana image at the Lion Gate (Singhadwara)
Ashtadhyayi 8.4.45 (a stop before a nasal may become nasal): jagannātha (jagat + nātha)

notes: Written fresh for year 5 (Sanskrit for readers, 'sandhi plainly'). Takes consonant sandhi with final t.
Ashtadhyayi 8.4.45 (yaro 'nunāsike 'nunāsiko vā), 8.2.39 (jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte) and 8.4.40 (stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ) cited for t before n, before voiced sounds, and before c. Confirm.
saccidānanda: sat + cit gives sac-cit; cit + ānanda gives cid-ānanda. Confirm the spoken explanation ('before the vowel the t takes on voice').
Jagannath worshipped at Puri, Odisha, as lord of the world: confirm phrasing.

2026-10-15 quality pass: failed the test (consonant sandhi with a self-help 'today': adjust to the person beside you, stay yourself; the chat was about a speaking slot). Rewritten: story is Puri's Indradyumna legend (the log, the carver behind the closed door, the unfinished images, 'worship them as they are'), told 'as Puri tells it' because versions differ (the carver is Vishwakarma or Vishnu in disguise in different tellings; the number of days varies, so none is given); teaching is Jagannath as lord of the world who comes out at Rath Yatra so anyone may see him and pull the ropes, with chhera pahara (the king sweeping the chariot). The jagat + natha sandhi stays; sadguru and sacchidananda were dropped (the notes above on 8.2.39, 8.4.40 and saccidananda are now historical; 1455's recall updated to match). Practice: picture the Grand Road, 'Jai Jagannath' or a non-praying option. New title and carry; chat (Sam sees a Rath Yatra downtown) tests the teaching and has a tie; Priya's slot-after-Sam thread dropped.
